items.title: Antonelli leads a Mercedes one-two in Qatar FP1
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli set the fastest time in the first Qatar practice session at 1:23.217. George Russell was second, 0.507 seconds behind, and Isack Hadjar third, 0.661 seconds back. The official FIA classification matches Formula1.com across all 22 entrants.
items.why_it_matters: This is the first completed on-track classification of the weekend. It is practice form only, not a qualifying or race prediction.

items.title: FIA summons Red Bull representative over Hadjar pit-lane incident
items.summary: FIA Document 15, issued at 17:18 local, summons the Red Bull team representative to report to the Stewards at 18:15 after an alleged unsafe situation involving team personnel in the pit lane at 16:45. It cites Article 12.2.1.h of the FIA International Sporting Code and records an allegation, not a finding or penalty.
items.why_it_matters: Keep this separate from a driver sanction and check the official FIA listing for any later ruling after the summons time.

items.title: Qatar's 27-lap cap, pressure rules and allocation conflict
items.summary: FIA competition visa confirms a 57-lap race. Pirelli set a 27-lap maximum per set and selected C1/C2/C3. FIA Document 13 V2 specifies the latest counting and replacement instructions; its pressure table gives minimum starting pressures of 29.0 psi front and 27.5 psi rear, with higher stabilized thresholds. Two Formula1.com articles still conflict on the individual pre-event set allocation (2/3/8 plus a Q3 Soft versus 2/4/7); Pirelli has not resolved those totals. The official Formula1.com explainer says cumulative set mileage includes Safety Car and Virtual Safety Car laps. Remaining sets require a separate post-qualifying source.
items.why_it_matters: Do not turn either pre-event allocation report into a remaining-set count or a strategy prediction. Apply the current FIA V2 rules and preserve the unresolved allocation conflict.

items.title: The titles are settled; Red Bull and McLaren are nine points apart for P3
items.summary: After Las Vegas, Formula1.com lists Kimi Antonelli on 402 points to Max Verstappen’s 304 and Mercedes on 666 points; both championships have already been decided. Red Bull has 440 points and McLaren 431 in the Constructors’ standings, a nine-point gap for third.
items.why_it_matters: The remaining constructors’ battle is live context for Qatar; do not present settled titles as still contested or confuse current totals with a pre-event snapshot.

items.title: Verstappen/Russell tension and Ferrari clash follow F1 to Qatar
items.summary: Formula1.com's 25 November Qatar preview recounts the continuing Verstappen-Russell verbal dispute and Ferrari's Las Vegas fallout: Charles Leclerc hit team-mate Lewis Hamilton during their Turn 7 fight. FIA Document 60 found Leclerc wholly responsible and imposed a 10-second penalty; team principal Fred Vasseur described the incident as unacceptable. At Thursday's FIA press conference, Leclerc said Ferrari needed a solution, accepted responsibility for the Vegas clash, and declined to disclose whether the rules of engagement would change. He also denied having a contractual number-one clause. Neither statement establishes the team's operational race instructions. A 26 November media-day report quotes Hamilton saying securing second in the Constructors' Championship is Ferrari's immediate priority, the drivers remain free to race, and process/communication improvements will be discussed over winter. The Race's Qatar day-one report says Antonelli described a Mercedes software safety feature added after the Vegas battery-deployment loss; this is a reported team change, not a change to FIA limits or a validated Qatar outcome. Formula1.com's Russell/Verstappen update adds that Russell found some post-race comments "quite amusing", is moving on and does not want to continue the off-track exchange; Verstappen said there was nothing else to add and that his focus was Qatar.
items.why_it_matters: The Vegas penalty is final and does not become a Qatar ruling. Leclerc's contract denial and the drivers' comments do not establish team race instructions or a new rule. Attribute the Mercedes software update to The Race; do not treat it as an FIA energy-limit change or a confirmed on-track result. Keep Russell and Verstappen quotes attributed, not as predictions.
